title: Engineering notebook: choose the page's working grammar
question: You already pinned the world: off-white or near-black, a contemporary sans with a mono for figures, and sage as the only accent. These cards decide the structure it's built from. Keep the roll, take my pick, or re-roll.

options.label: Press proof sheet
options.lineage: print-manufacturing press proofs: crop marks, slug line, colour bar, sign-off
options.thesis: The CV presented as a signed-off proof from the print and manufacturing world Josh builds software for.
options.viewport: Name and role inside hairline crop marks; a mono slug line (name · CV · updated Sep 2026); the animated strip sits where a press colour bar would, carrying the 3-item proof strip; Email me and LinkedIn below.
options.risk: Could read as a print designer's portfolio, and it ties the identity to CPI's industry rather than to Josh.

raised.raise: Exactly four tones per theme; no fifth colour anywhere.
The animated strip rests when idle, wakes under the pointer, then fades back.
Every role is deep-linkable, and the nav shows the active section.
The close is a real destination: a sign-off block, not a footer afterthought.
Every text block has a set line length (about 68 characters maximum).

options.label: Drawing title block and revision table
options.lineage: ISO engineering-drawing title blocks and revision tables
options.thesis: Career as a revision history, and Drawn → Checked → Approved as a leader who still builds.
options.viewport: The hero is a ruled title block: Name / Role / Org / Location / Rev cells beside the portrait; the proof strip sits on the animated band as the drawing's key figures; below, a revision table runs from Sep 2017 to Manager in May 2025.
options.risk: My top-ranked candidate, and literal field labels can tip into costume if they're overdone.

options.label: Four-shade handheld field
options.viewport: A 160x144 framed field with the CV as tile text.
options.case: Loses on both axes: senior hiring readers see a novelty, and the pixel type hurts clarity.
options.kept: Total palette discipline: four tones, no fifth.

options.label: Teen-magazine quiz spread
options.thesis: A quiz that ends in a verdict box.
options.viewport: Collaged columns running down to a verdict box.
options.case: Loses on both axes: the tone is wrong for the audience.
options.kept: The close is a destination, not a footer.

options.label: Bioluminescent wake
options.thesis: Light that answers motion, then fades.
options.viewport: A dark field lit by pointer wakes.
options.case: Loses on both axes: it's atmosphere, not proof.
options.kept: Motion is a response that returns to rest.

options.label: Coiled earth tower
options.viewport: Horizontal text courses rising up the page.
options.case: Loses on both axes: there's no link to Josh's world.
options.kept: Every line length is set on purpose.

options.label: HyperCard stack
options.thesis: Linked cards that you read and edit in the same place.
options.case: Loses on both axes: nostalgia over clarity for recruiters.
options.kept: Every card is addressable; back retraces your path.

options.label: Darkroom safelight bay
options.viewport: Stations running in fixed order under amber light.
options.case: Loses on both axes: the palette breaks your pinned world and the metaphor is unrelated.
options.kept: A fixed reading order: level first, then detail.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean single-column developer CV, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name, title, one line and buttons, with the portrait at the right; timeline below.
canonCard.risk: Hard to tell apart from every other engineer's site.
